## November 3 evening report and its first-part copy

**Sources on this page:** p111 A1. [Concise case study](../military/nov3_evening_report.md).

**Shared edition.** The following reading also discusses [p112 A1](112.md#source-p112-a1), [p112 A2](112.md#source-p112-a2), [p112 A3](112.md#source-p112-a3).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov3-evening-report-november-3-evening-report-and-its-first-part-copy"></a>



**Status:** four physical records: the first-part witness on p111 and all
three source-marked parts on p112. The two first parts support seventeen
previously erased coordinates, while two observed coordinate conflicts
remain explicit. The damaged second and third parts have separately priced
editorial readings and three unresolved positions.

The p112 header gives an origin of 2030 (3), a receipt of 2.33 a.m. on
November 4 and three parts. The p111 witness is received at 3.44 a.m. on
November 4; its sender is missing and its recipient is NKJ. Both pages are
headed November 3. The source images are [p111](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p111_full.png)
and [p112](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/sources/p112_full.png).

The readable passages retain every edited label other than X separators;
case, punctuation and German umlaut/ss display forms are normalized.
A separate character-level mapping checks this correspondence. The literal
`A`, doubled separator, strange date/reference labels and repeated `TLICH`
remain. No abbreviation is expanded into a person's identity.

### p111 A1

The source has 202 slots, including three complete five-dash groups. All fifteen source-mask fills are supplied by the p112 witness. The single observed repair selects UJVIDEK at its first occurrence; the second occurrence is unchanged in both copies.

### p112 A1

This source also has 202 slots. Visible C in XGCXV and R in AARVA remain literal invalid-coordinate glyphs; the other copy supplies G and F. The ordinary DONOU → DONAU repair is separate.

<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

```

```

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> OKM. OKM. Abendmeldung. An Save, Donau Ruhe. Alp. Korps erreicht Raum südlich Ujvidek. Ujvidek. 219219IDU. G. K. 5353.

The candidate uses **1 observed-coordinate substitution**, **2 source-mask fills** and **0 unprinted-coordinate fills**. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

There are **183 identical observed coordinates**, seventeen one-sided
erasures and two conflicting observed coordinates. All four common streams
have the same minimum combined cost of two observed substitutions. The
chosen readable stream selects DONAU from p111 and UJVIDEK from p112;
copying alone does not make either conflicting value unanimous.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov3-evening-report-p112-a2"></a>

### p112 A2

The native 218-slot source includes four complete five-dash groups. The older OCR lost one entire group and produced a misleading 213-slot frame. This is the most editorially uncertain part: the raw JAEVZE?G and ?ELLRA? are not independently proved to be FAHRZEUG and BELGRAD. Their repairs are priced, and two reference positions remain unknown.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — native source frame:**

```text
??ETENAX41??X11XMAD??HNACHNOR??STENANXX?UFTAUFKLA?RUNGXSTA?KENJAEVZE?GVERK?HR?SEMEN?RIA?ELLRA?XG?NXSTA?SXO?FZ
```

**Edited output — priced editorial candidate under the same stated frame:**

```text
TRETENAX41??X11XMARSCHNACHNORDOSTENANXXLUFTAUFKLAERUNGXSTARKENFAHRZEUGVERKEHRXSEMENDRIABELGRADXGENXSTABSXOFFZ
```

</details>

**Readable German — based on the edited candidate above; the local qualifications remain in force:**

> Treten A 41?? / 11. Marsch nach Nordosten an. Luftaufklärung starken Fahrzeugverkehr Semendria Belgrad. Gen. Stabs. Offz.

The candidate uses **6 observed-coordinate substitutions**, **18 source-mask fills** and **0 unprinted-coordinate fills**. Its remaining zero-based plaintext-position domains are `10: 569PTX`, `11: 248CIM`. These are literal square labels, without an additional historical numeral assignment.

The earlier **FLUGZEUG** candidate is retained in the [alternative ledger](../../experiments/nov3_evening_and_nov4_radio/editorial_alternatives.json).
Independent review found that **FAHRZEUG** reduces the observed-coordinate
cost from ten to six while keeping all eighteen source-mask fills and both
reference unknowns. This comparison favors the displayed candidate without
proving that every word is uniquely historical. No missing reporting verb
is added to the stream or the readable display.

## p111 B — Use radio for important messages

**Sources on this page:** p111 B. [Concise case study](../radio/p111_B.md).

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p111-b-p111-b--use-radio-for-important-messages"></a>


[Case guide](../README.md) · [ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [Source image](../../sources/excerpts/other_p111_B.png) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Status:** A complete direct reading of a supplementary message. The unchanged
published `Nov1-3` key fixes **all 154 plaintext positions** and reproduces all
**308 source coordinates**. No source coordinate, key cell or message length
is changed.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p111-b-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Readable German:**

> Fuer Chef Mittelmeerdivision, B. M. K., Nateko:
> Wegen Unsicherheit der Kabelverbindungen fuer wichtige Mel[d]ungen
> Funkspruch benutzen. Admiralstab 18266 D, roem. 2.

**Meaning:** Addressed to the chief of the Mediterranean Division, B.M.K. and
Nateko: because cable connections are unreliable, use radio for important
messages. The message closes with an Admiralty Staff reference, `18266 D`,
followed by the instruction to read `2` as a Roman numeral.

The body provides a direct reason for using radio: uncertainty about the
cable connections. It does not specify whether this was caused by physical
damage, interception, censorship or some other problem. `B. M. K.` and
`NATEKO` are retained as decoded abbreviations, without an unverified expansion.

The only supplied letter in the displayed reading is the bracketed `d` in
*Meldungen*. The raw text spells the word **`MELUNGEN`**. That spelling omission
is kept in the cryptographic transcript and is not counted as an extra
recovered position. Spacing, capitalization and punctuation are editorial.

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p111-b-exact-direct-reading"></a>

### Exact direct reading

<details>
<summary>Raw decoded text</summary>

**Raw output:**

```text
FUERXCHEFXMITTELMEERDIVISIONXBXMXKXNATEKOXWEGENXUNSICHERHEITXDERXKABELVERBINDUNGENXFUERXWICHTIGEXMELUNGENXFUNKSPRUCHXBENUTZENXADMIRALSTABX18266XDXROEMX2XX
```

</details>

Every letter and digit in this string is fixed by the source and the complete
published key. Re-encryption reproduces the literal source exactly, including
the spelling `MELUNGEN`. The `X` characters act as separators here; `ROEMX2`
is the direct text behind the rendered “roem. 2.”

<a id="edition-cases-radio-p111-b-source-and-dates"></a>

### Source and dates

Printed p111 / PDF p114, section B. The page heading is **3 November 1918**,
and the internal stamp is `2315 (3.11)`. The reception header actually prints
`FUER NKJ, ASO, RAT v LP (2.54 a.m., November 5th); RICHI-308`.
The differing dates are visible in the source and are retained without
inferring a cause or silently changing either date.

The [literal source record](../../experiments/corpus_readings/selected_sources.json)
contains all grouped coordinates. The
[certificate](../../experiments/corpus_readings/certificates.json) gives every
plaintext position's source pair, the key provenance, an independent
column-offset inverse and the exact re-encryption check.

```sh
python3 experiments/corpus_readings/verify.py --verify
```

**Credit:** George Lasry's published period key and its historical sources are
